text: Who qualifies for the subsidized fertilizer? A duly registered farmer whose details are in the register provided to National Cereals & Produce Board (NCPB) qualifies.
What do I need to be able to buy subsidized fertilizer? You need to appear in person at the nearest NCPB depot with your original identity card and your name must be in the register.
Can I buy subsidized fertilizer on behalf of somebody else? No, that is not acceptable.
What if am not registered? You are requested to visit your County or Sub county or Ward Agricultural Office for registration.
Do I need to pay for registration as a farmer? No, registration is free of charge. You only need to visit the nearest County, Sub-county or ward Agricultural Office.
Where can I get the fertilizer from? You can get the subsidized fertilizer from any of the nearest NCPB depots within the county where you are registered.

How many bags of fertilizer can a farmer buy? Each registered farmer is entitled to a combined maximum of 100 bags for both planting and top-dressing fertilizer per season depending on the registered acreage. A farmer is allowed two bags each for planting and top dressing per acre.

How much do I pay for the subsidized fertilizers? Approved subsidized fertilizer selling price per 50kg bag (Kshs.): DAP 3,500; NPKs 3,275; MOP 1,775; UREA 3,500; CAN 2,875; Local Blends 3,275; Sulphate of Ammonia 2,220.
How do I make the payment? M-pesa through the NCPB Till Number displayed at the Depot, or bank deposit as provided by the Depot/Silo Manager. Cash payments at the depot shall NOT be accepted.
Can a farmer buy on credit? No, farmers are required to pay before collecting the fertilizer.
Can one buy the fertilizer and resell to others? NO, this is ILLEGAL.
At what time can I buy the fertilizer? All NCPB depots are open Monday to Friday from 8.00am to 5.00pm.
The price of government subsidized fertilizer will remain at an affordable Ksh 2,500 per 50-kg bag this season, ensuring that more farmers benefit from this program.

To enhance accessibility, the government is increasing the number of outlets through partnerships with cooperatives and agro-vet stores, in addition to the existing NCPB depots. Registered farmers will receive e-vouchers, which they can redeem at these outlets.

The subsidized fertilizer is being sold at a reduced price of Sh2,500 from the original price of Sh6,500 at either National Cereals and Produce Board (NCPB) or Kenya National Trading Corporation (KNTC) stores.
Registered farmers purchase fertiliser at Ksh 2,500 per 50-kilogram bag through an E-voucher system and redeem it at designated collection centres across the county.

The fertiliser is now available at 16 county-managed collection centres, in addition to four NCPB outlets, bringing the total number of collection points to 20. Registered farmers are encouraged to collect their fertiliser at the designated collection point nearest to them.

Following the Government's latest price reduction, farmers can now purchase the subsidized fertilizer at KSh 2,000 per 50kg bag, making farm inputs more affordable as farmers prepare for the short rains.
A total of 16 stores have been identified as fertilizer distribution points across the County, bringing subsidized farm inputs closer to farmers.

The Government through the Ministry of Agriculture has assured farmers in the lower Eastern Regions of Machakos, Kitui and Makueni counties of the availability of enough subsidised fertiliser at the four allocated depots in Machakos.
